support_spans: compound heterozygous alterations (c.2992 + 2T>G and c.8621-30A>G) at splice sites in COL7A1
Immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy of the grafted area showed type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils
concepts.why: The presence of a large unhealed ulcer, compound heterozygous alterations in COL7A1, and the presence of type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils on immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy are characteristic of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.

contradict_spans: compound heterozygous alterations (c.2992 + 2T>G and c.8621-30A>G) at splice sites in COL7A1
concepts.why: While the presence of a large unhealed ulcer could suggest Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa, the compound heterozygous alterations in COL7A1 are more characteristic of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.

contradict_spans: compound heterozygous alterations (c.2992 + 2T>G and c.8621-30A>G) at splice sites in COL7A1
concepts.why: While the presence of a large unhealed ulcer could suggest Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex, the compound heterozygous alterations in COL7A1 are more characteristic of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.

contradict_spans: compound heterozygous alterations (c.2992 + 2T>G and c.8621-30A>G) at splice sites in COL7A1
concepts.why: While the presence of a large unhealed ulcer could suggest Kindler Syndrome, the compound heterozygous alterations in COL7A1 are more characteristic of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
The presence of a large unhealed ulcer is not characteristic of Pseudoxanthoma Elasticum, which is typically associated with skin laxity and calcification of elastic fibers.

The presence of dominant RNA transcripts with premature stop codons and rare wild-type reads in affected skin epidermis, along with compound heterozygous COL7A1 alterations, explains the persistent ulcer and skin blistering.
